title: Finite presentation of a ring map glues on target principal opens
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Let $s\subseteq S$ generate the unit ideal: every element of $S$ is a finite sum of multiples of elements of $s$. For $g\in s$ write $S_g=S[1/g]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], regarded as an $R$-algebra through $R\to S\to S_g$. If every composite $R\to S_g$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], then $R\to S$ is of finite presentation. The set $s$ may be infinite or empty; in the latter case its unit-ideal hypothesis forces $S=0$.
